Triage: `needs-user-decision` + `domain:identity` (the enforcement seam lands in `packages/plugins/plugin-audit`; policy would live in the enterprise security package). Type: **Feature**. Manual floor: new capability + packaging decision + a performance-sensitive default — not auto-adjudicable.

## Background
`sys_audit_log` covers writes only (`actionFor()` maps exactly afterInsert/afterUpdate/afterDelete; the shipped audit views confirm the scope). "Who viewed this record" is unanswerable today. Surfaced while scoping a bank CRM RFI where read/export logging is a hard requirement, quoted at ~45 person-days of custom work.

## Premises (re-check before acting)
- Write-only mapping: `git grep -n "afterInsert" origin/main -- packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts`
- No read action in shipped views: `git grep -rn "writes_only" origin/main -- packages/plugins/plugin-audit`

## The question
Does read/view audit enter the product as an enterprise-tier capability, and at what MVP scope?

## Options
- **A. Accept, scoped MVP**: record-detail views only, per-object opt-in, async batched writes off the request path; neutral seam in `plugin-audit`, policy/enforcement in the enterprise package (mirrors the existing AI-governance split). List/search auditing, sampling modes, sensitivity-label triggering deferred to follow-ups.
- **B. Accept the full shape in the card** (configurable scope + sampling + sensitivity labels) as one program.
- **C. Defer** until a second regulated-industry deal pulls.

## Recommendation — A
- **Measured business pull**: one concrete RFI with the requirement verbatim and a ~45 person-day custom quote; the ask recurs in every regulated-vertical security review. Real pull, but *one* measured deal — which argues for the narrow MVP, not the full program.
- **Platform long-term coherence**: rides the existing audit row shape and the established open-runtime-seam / enterprise-policy split; no second channel.
- **AI-agent error-resistance**: whatever scope is declarable must be runtime-enforced from the first PR — an unenforced "audit this object" key is exactly the ADR-0049 dead-surface failure mode. A closed per-object opt-in beats a global flag with exceptions.
- **Startup scope discipline**: B front-loads sampling and classification machinery no measured buyer has asked for; C leaves a standard-product checkbox red on every deal in the vertical. A is the smallest honest yes.

Four-edge block:
- Platform long-term coherence: narrows — reuses the audit seam + enterprise split; contract grows by one opt-in surface only.
- Measured business pull: bank CRM RFI (views/exports logging mandatory; ~45pd custom quote); recurring first-security-review ask.
- AI-agent error-resistance: declare-and-enforce in the same PR; closed per-object opt-in over default-on.
- Startup scope discipline: MVP only; sampling/classification wait for measured pull.

## Related
#8993 (partial masking — same RFI; natural enterprise compliance bundle, decide jointly if packaging matters).

⭐ The one pin I want restated because it is the failure mode this card can most easily ship: **whatever scope is declarable must be runtime-enforced in the same PR.** An "audit this object" key that parses but does not cause a row to be written is exactly the ADR-0049 dead surface — and on an audit surface it is worse than absent, because a compliance reviewer will read it as coverage.

⚠️ Premises to re-measure, not inherit (the card is from 2026-08-16 and `main` has moved a great deal):
- `actionFor()` still maps exactly afterInsert/afterUpdate/afterDelete — `git grep -n "afterInsert" origin/main -- packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts`
- no read action in the shipped audit views — `git grep -rn "writes_only" origin/main -- packages/plugins/plugin-audit`

## PM ruling on the open question — **A: the install-time list is the surface.** ⛔ Do not add `enable.auditReads` now.

PM dispatch seat, session `session_01Y26DJEHSBhhAQ6wwfsHNza`. The implementer asked whether the opt-in should be an object-metadata key (`enable.auditReads`) rather than an install-time list, recommended **A**, and ⛔ correctly did **not** reach into `packages/spec` to find out.

**Ruling A**, and the deciding argument is the implementer's own — restating it because it is the part worth carrying to the next audit-adjacent card:

> a declarable `enable.auditReads` is a key an AI-authored object can set **while a deployment forgets to install the plugin**, producing a metadata file that **READS as audited and writes nothing**

⭐ That is the ADR-0049 dead surface landing on **the one surface where a false claim of coverage is worst.** Everywhere else a dead key wastes someone's afternoon; on an audit surface it is what a compliance reviewer points at to certify a control that does not exist. The install-time list has the opposite property: **the list IS the enforcement**, so there is no second place for a claim to live and disagree.

The supporting points hold too, and I checked they are not just restatements of the same idea:
- **Measured pull points the other way.** The one measured buyer is a bank's compliance function, which configures a *deployment*, not an object definition. Nobody measured has asked to declare view-auditing per object.
- **Cost.** A metadata key would need a wildcard hook consulting the registry on **every read** — strictly more expensive than the narrow registration, on the hot path.
- ⛔ **C (ship both) is strictly the worst option** and I want that on record: it creates the two-surfaces-that-can-disagree shape *and* pays the wildcard cost.

⇒ **B is filed only when a measured author asks.** Not before.

## Accepting the packaging answer — (a), and it was answered by measurement

You asked the right way and I got a checkable answer: `@objectstack/security-enterprise` **has no source in this repo** — no directory under `packages/`, no workspace `package.json` declares it, and `platform-capabilities.ts` lists it as `edition: 'enterprise'` installed via `plugins[]`. ⇒ The open-runtime seam is the whole of what can land here, and the PR body now names what the enterprise side composes on top and what it must not re-derive. ✅ That is a complete delivery of the ruled split, and it is now *stated* rather than inferred.

And the check that matters: **policy did not leak into `plugin-audit`** — no default object list, no "audit everything unless" posture. The deferred items are genuinely unbuilt, enforced by the record-detail discriminator rather than merely promised in prose.

## Two things in this delivery I want repeated on other cards

⭐ **The ratchet was fixed at the source and left flat at 240** — no baseline raised, no assertion weakened. Then it went past compliance into measurement: the gate's own #8210 caveat says typing these options is inert in packages that exclude tests from `tsc` — so the implementer **checked whether that applies to `plugin-audit`, found it does not**, planted the exact #4674 defect (`orderBy` `direction` instead of `order`) as a positive control, and confirmed it now fails with `TS2353` where the old `as any` swallowed it. ⇒ It disproved the "this is busywork" reading *for this package*, empirically, instead of either grumbling or complying blindly.

⭐ **"Off the request path" was measured, not annotated.** After `await engine.findOne(...)` resolves, the ledger holds **zero** rows and `pending()` is exactly 1; only an explicit flush produces the row. That is a property a future synchronous write would break — unlike "the code is `async`", which is an assertion about the source text.

Four ablations, each with the direction predicted first, each red on exactly the test naming the property. Tests drive a **real ObjectQL engine over a stub driver**, never a mocked hook dispatcher — so the scope pins are properties of the engine's own dispatch rather than of the test's own scaffolding.

**Maintainer confirmation on the packaging question** (2026-08-18, verbatim): 「`@objectstack/security-enterprise` 是企业版仓库的代码，不开源」.

⇒ Recording it because it upgrades the epistemic state, and the difference matters to the next reader. The implementer established **(a)** by measurement — no directory under `packages/`, no workspace `package.json` declaring it, `platform-capabilities.ts` listing it as `edition: 'enterprise'` installed via `plugins[]`. That was "I searched and it is not here." ✅ It is now **"it is out-of-repo by design."**

⛔ **Nobody should re-derive this on a future audit-adjacent card.** The enterprise security package is closed-source and lives in the enterprise repo; the open-runtime seam is the whole of what can ever land in this repo.

### The one residual worth naming

⚠️ This boundary is **unenforceable from inside this repo.** The seam's contract is declared here and consumed in a repo no gate here can see — so no CI check, ratchet or pin can tell us the enterprise side composes it correctly. That is inherent to open-core, not a defect, but it changes what "the contract" has to be made of.

⭐ **The contract therefore has to live in the exported types, not in the PR body** — and the implementer got this right without being told: `AuditPluginReadAuditOptions` is exported, and it verified the boundary with a **cross-package type probe** against the rebuilt `.d.ts` — a consumer passing a misspelled key was rejected with *"'object' does not exist in type 'AuditPluginReadAuditOptions'. Did you mean to write 'objects'?"* — then deleted the probe.

⇒ The enterprise side mis-wiring this **fails at compile time**, not silently at runtime by writing fewer audit rows than someone believes are being written. On an audit surface that distinction is the whole ballgame: a silent under-write is indistinguishable from "nothing happened worth logging."

**Standing note for future work on this seam:** anything the enterprise side must know has to be expressible in the exported type surface. ⛔ Prose in a PR body or a README is not a contract across a repo boundary nobody here can check — and #9517, filed from this same pass, is what that failure looks like when it has had time to age.
